page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-384 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the g4 server family. It is equipped with 384 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and 1440.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. The primary hardware feature of this instance is the inclusion of eight bundled NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 graphics processing units. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given its high-density GPU configuration and massive vCPU count, this instance represents a premium hardware class designed for extreme parallel processing workloads. The absence of local storage means that data persistence and high-speed scratch space must be handled via network-attached storage, which introduces potential network I/O considerations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the consolidation of eight enterprise-grade GPUs and 384 vCPUs into a single virtual machine minimizes inter-node communication latency compared to multi-node clusters, making it highly resource-dense for large-scale operations. This server type is designed for workloads such as intensive 3D rendering, large-scale computer-aided engineering, deep learning training, high-throughput video transcoding, and complex scientific simulations.
